summary: Mozambique waives visas for SADC citizens and, since a 2023 decree, for about 30 major tourism-source countries including the US, Australia and much of Western Europe (30 days, with a small processing fee), while British and Canadian citizens need a paid Electronic Travel Authorization and other nationalities can obtain a simplified tourist visa at the border or apply online.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in Maputo hotels, supermarkets and the bigger beach lodges; everywhere else cash rules. US dollars and South African rand are widely taken in tourist areas, but carry small metical notes up-country.

safety.text: The southern and central tourist areas — Maputo, Inhambane, Tofo, Vilankulo and the Bazaruto archipelago — are generally calm, though petty crime and police document checks are common. Avoid Cabo Delgado province in the far north, where an armed insurgency continues, and the Memba and Eráti districts of Nampula and the Mecula and Marrupa districts of Niassa.

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the dry, cooler season — ideal for beaches, diving and safaris. November to April is hot and humid, with cyclone risk along the coast roughly January to March.

tips.text: Avoid Cabo Delgado province in the far north, where an insurgency continues, including Pemba's surroundings when advisories say so. The main beach destinations from Maputo up to Vilankulo are far from the affected area.
Carry your passport with entry stamp (or a notarised copy) at all times — police checkpoints are frequent and fines for missing documents are common.
If you need a border visa, bring the fee in US dollar cash — card terminals at land borders are unreliable. Rand are usually accepted at crossings from South Africa and Eswatini.
Cyclone and heavy-rain season runs roughly December to March, especially along the central and northern coast — roads flood and ferries stop. Check forecasts if traveling in that window.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mozambique?
faq.answer: Many tourists no longer need a visa. SADC citizens enter free, and under a 2023 decree citizens of about 30 major tourism-source countries — including the US, Portugal and most of Western Europe — enter visa-free for up to 30 days. British and Canadian citizens must first obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online. Everyone else can get a simplified tourist visa at the border or apply online at evisa.gov.mz.

faq.question: What is the border fee for visa-free visitors?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt tourists under the 2023 scheme pay a MZN 650 processing fee (about USD 10). Decree 10/2023 sets it as payable when pre-registering at evisa.gov.mz at least 48 hours before boarding, so register and pay online before you fly. Mozambique's High Commission in London describes it as paid on arrival, so carry some cash too — meticais, dollars or rand are normally accepted.

faq.question: Can I get a Mozambique visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Mozambique's border visa allows two entries and 30 days, cannot be extended, and is paid in cash (no official source publishes the amount), but the migration service issues it mainly to nationals of countries where Mozambique has no embassy or consulate, or on reciprocity. Applying in advance through evisa.gov.mz is the safer route, especially if you arrive at a small crossing.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Mozambique?
faq.answer: Yes — tourist stays can normally be extended once, for up to 30 further days, at migration service (migração) offices in provincial capitals, though the border visa issued on arrival cannot be extended. Apply before your current permission expires; overstays are fined per day.

faq.question: Is Mozambique safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The main beach circuit in the south and center is generally fine with normal precautions. The serious security problem is confined to Cabo Delgado province in the far north. Check current advisories, carry your documents, and avoid driving at night.
